analysis.investment_thesis: Finolex Cables is a fundamentally sound, debt-free industrial compounder, but at a 3.8% earnings yield (EBIT ₹543 Cr / EV ₹14,315 Cr) it fails the Magic Formula's basic cheapness test. ROCE of 17.7% is respectable but not exceptional enough to justify paying 21x earnings.
key_strengths: Pristine balance sheet: virtually zero debt (₹20 Cr total debt vs ₹5,703 Cr equity), giving massive financial flexibility
Infrastructure-linked revenue: 9.4% revenue CAGR (₹2,360→₹5,319 Cr) supported by India's electrification and housing buildout
Large investment portfolio generating ₹428 Cr other income (FY25), acting as a hidden earnings buffer
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~3.8% (EBIT/EV) is well below the 6% Magic Formula floor — the stock simply isn't cheap
Operating margin of 8.9% is thin and the operating income CAGR (4.7% over 9Y) trails revenue (9.4%) — margin compression is a structural concern
Heavy non-operating income dependency: other income (₹428 Cr) is 79% of operating income (₹543 Cr), making reported earnings unreliable as a quality signal
red_flags: FY25 Free Cash Flow collapsed to ₹207 Cr from ₹577 Cr in FY24, driven by capex surge to ₹236 Cr (CWIP jumped to ₹303 Cr) — FCF quality is deteriorating
Other income (₹428 Cr) is nearly equal to operating income (₹543 Cr); strip it out and this looks like a low-margin, slow-growth industrial at a premium valuation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Finolex yields disappointing results on the 'cheap' leg. Enterprise Value is approximately ₹14,315 Cr (market cap ₹14,385 Cr + debt ₹20 Cr − cash ₹90 Cr). FY25 EBIT (operating income) is ₹543 Cr, giving an earnings yield of just 3.8% — far below the 12% I look for and even below the minimum 6% threshold. If I generously include normalized other income (e.g., ₹300 Cr), the blended yield reaches ~6% but that involves crediting volatile investment returns, which the Magic Formula explicitly avoids. On the quality leg, reported ROCE of 17.7% is decent but not in the top-decile 25%+ zone. Operating margins at 8.9% are thin for a branded electrical goods company, and the 9-year operating income CAGR of 4.7% trails revenue at 9.4% — not a hallmark of a high-return compounder.

The structural story is sound: zero-debt, India's infrastructure capex cycle, a diversified product portfolio from cables to fans and switchgear. But the balance sheet is inflated by a massive equity investment portfolio that distorts both the ROE (13.4% understates true operating returns) and the earnings quality (FY25 other income of ₹428 Cr nearly matches operating income). The capex ramp (₹219 Cr in FY24, ₹236 Cr in FY25, CWIP surging to ₹303 Cr) could seed future growth but is crushing near-term FCF (down 64% YoY to ₹207 Cr). At P/E 21x and EV/EBITDA 19x, the market is pricing in a lot of good news. Magic Formula discipline says wait for the price to come to you.
